heroLead: Guilford Lake is better known for its state park than for oil and gas, but the mineral rights underneath the surrounding land are just as real as anywhere else in the county.
intro: Guilford Lake sits in Columbiana County, an area more associated with the state park and recreational land around it than with drilling activity, though mineral ownership under the surrounding farmland is common and often overlooked by families who've held it for generations. Like most of Columbiana County, this area sits on the flank of the Utica/Point Pleasant fairway, where development has been more selective than in the core counties to the south.

sections.heading: Recreational land and mineral rights don't always move together
paragraphs: Land near Guilford Lake that's used recreationally or held for its scenic value can still carry a mineral reservation from decades earlier, since surface use and mineral ownership are entirely separate legal questions. A family that's owned lake-adjacent land for generations may not realize the oil and gas rights were severed from the surface long before the current owners had any connection to the property.

sections.heading: What to check before assuming your minerals are inactive
paragraphs: With limited drilling activity directly around Guilford Lake, most unleased interests here haven't generated royalty income, but that doesn't mean they lack value. A title search through the Columbiana County Recorder's office in Lisbon will confirm whether a severance occurred, whether a lease has ever been recorded, and who currently holds the interest.

faqs.question: Does owning recreational or lake-adjacent land affect mineral ownership?
faqs.answer: Not directly. Surface use, whether recreational or agricultural, is separate from mineral ownership, which depends entirely on whether and how the minerals were severed in the chain of title.

faqs.question: Is there drilling activity near Guilford Lake?
faqs.answer: This part of Columbiana County sits on the Utica flank, so development has generally been limited compared to core counties, though it's worth checking your specific township.

faqs.question: How do I find out if my minerals were ever severed from the surface?
faqs.answer: A title search at the Columbiana County Recorder's office, tracing your deed back through prior conveyances, will show whether a severance deed exists and what it reserved.

faqs.question: What documents should I gather if I want to sell an unleased interest?
faqs.answer: Your deed or the original severance instrument, plus any family paperwork referencing oil or gas rights, even informal notes, since they can speed up a title search considerably.
